attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: A faithful observation that, as of the post, neither GPT-5 nor Sora had been publicly released.

contract.note: Reading 'dropped/shipped' as public release, not red-team or artist previews, is the ordinary reading. It matters because Sora had restricted access.

evidence.note: On Dec 9, 2024 OpenAI says it is moving Sora out of research preview and 'releasing it today'. That implies Sora was not publicly available on Sept 25, 2024.
OpenAI introduced GPT-5 on Aug 7, 2025, which implies it had not been released by Sept 2024.
From Feb 2024 only red teamers and selected artists had access. That is a restricted preview, not a public release.
Published on the target day. It reports Sora still in research mode in early September, with release still expected later.

reviews.rationale: Sora was public only from Dec 9, 2024; before that it was a restricted research preview (e3, e4). GPT-5 was introduced in Aug 2025. Together these show that neither product was publicly available on Sept 25, 2024. The restricted Sora access does not meet the contract's bar for a public release.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: A faithful present-tense observation that many lawsuits against OpenAI were pending.

contract.note: A threshold of at least five distinct pending actions, also checked with consolidated cases grouped, is a fair and ordinary reading of 'many'.

evidence.note: A Sept 13, 2024 SDNY order covers six case numbers, including the Authors Guild consolidated cases and CIR v. OpenAI, with ongoing discovery deadlines. Grouped, that is about three proceedings.
A Sept 15, 2024 status compilation shows Raw Story and Intercept v. OpenAI pending, with motions to dismiss unresolved. That makes at least five proceedings when grouped.

reviews.rationale: Court records and a dated status inventory show at least five pending actions against OpenAI in mid-September 2024. That holds even when consolidated cases are grouped (3 + 2). Eight distinct case numbers appear.

semantics.note: A faithful observation about the valuation being discussed in OpenAI's fundraising.

contract.note: Reading 'people are valuing' as investor negotiations at about $150B, with no completed deal required, is fair and ordinary.

evidence.note: A Sept 11, 2024 Reuters report, citing Bloomberg, says OpenAI was in talks to raise funds at a $150B valuation.

reviews.rationale: Contemporaneous reputable reporting within the target period shows fundraising negotiations valuing OpenAI at $150 billion, which matches the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'last year' and the $5b operating-loss figure, as the speaker stated them.

contract.note: Reading 'last year' as calendar 2023 is the ordinary reading for a Sept 2024 post. Leaving the accounting basis as unknown is fair.

evidence.note: This is a $1B projection for 2023, not a realized figure, and it notes that updated numbers were not disclosed. It cannot settle the claim.
The ~$5B figure is an expected loss for 2024, a different year and a projection. It is not the realized 2023 operating loss.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no realized 2023 operating-loss figure for OpenAI. The only 2023 number is a $1B projection, and the $5B figure refers to expected 2024 losses. Neither establishes or refutes the claim on a comparable basis.
